role: independent source/editorial check of proposed new composition and ungraded examples, before learner prose
independence: The actual Old English was translated and the solution saved in author-only-composition-solution.json before opening curriculum/proposals/unit07/author-only-models.json. Intended and independent readings then agreed; I want to help and I will help reflect willing intention in this context.

composition.coherence: The same two men and five animals continue throughout. The request, agreement, joint binding, payment in food, and resulting state form a connected episode. The first man's companion is naturally the second man in this scene.
prior_scope_checks: Two, five, first/second, man, animal, shore, companion, food, indicative narration, direct speech, personal objects/possessors, and ordinary helpan+dative are actually prior material.
Past-present vowel changes and forms were checked against the immutable actual registers, not inferred from familiarity with lemmas.
All 56 surface words have prior selected productive matches or explicit new Unit7 dependencies; this spelling check was supplemented by the contextual mood checks below.
new_dependencies: Gif as conditional conjunction and the explicitly taught contingent present construction.
Helpe is second-singular present subjunctive here; an earlier identical first-singular indicative spelling is not a prior milestone for that use.
Binden with wē is first-plural subjunctive exhortation.
Final wǣron bunden is a newly taught verbal passive with an uninflected participle; the earlier bare citation bunden did not teach that use.
semantic_limits: Wille states willing intention; the smooth English will help is a contextual promise, not evidence for a general future tense.
His gefēran is understandable in this episode, but his itself does not uniquely impose a reflexive antecedent.
The revised account omits narrative nū; it does not create a second now/then sense beyond the selected ordinary nū now.

teaching_examples.checks: Both phrases select masculine dative ðǣm sǣ already taught. Swimmað is assertion and swimmen a third-person plural wish.
Gāð is second-plural imperative; Gān wē is first-plural subjunctive exhortation. Surface gān previously known as infinitive does not establish the latter use.
Mæg ability, mōt permission and third-singular subjunctive swimme are kept semantically distinct.
Indicative open condition with hæfð and sęlð; personal recipient birds is dative and food accusative. Gif is not mechanically a subjunctive trigger.
Present contingent helpe plus indicative magon is a coherent request context; helpan takes dative mē and bindan accusative animals.

Cōme and hulpe are past subjunctives with the supplied unreal nonpast context. Their spellings overlap prior indicative second singulars; their actual third/first persons here are new. The interpretation must remain explicitly supported and recognition-only as declared.
Bindenda is the weak masculine nominative singular present participle after se. Strong predicate gōd is distinct. The example does not claim progressive be+participle teaching.

Cook§62 printed41/PDF57 explicitly permits an indeclinable verbal predicate or one ending like the strong masculine. Thus bunden and bundene with neuter plural dēor are admissible verbal-predicate realizations. The separately selected adjectival model U07-PART-BUNDEN gives strong neuter nominative/accusative plural bundenu and accepts bundene and bunden as variants under Cook§57.3 and the accompanying paradigm. Those adjective variants overlap the verbal-predicate spellings: spelling alone does not distinguish the constructions. The teaching distinction is that verbal predicates need not follow obligatory attributive agreement, not that bunden or bundene is invalid attributively.
teaching_examples.wording_reconciliation: Replaces the earlier inaccurate description of bunden as the single ordinary attributive neuter-plural cell; the reviewed example and verdict are unchanged.

teaching_examples.checks: Band is past3sg active; wearð bunden is a past event passive. The man is omitted in the passive; no untaught agent phrase is added.

Bēo geblētsod is second-singular passive imperative, with uninflected predicate avoiding invented addressee gender. Bēon birds gemanigfielde is third-plural wish with the verified source participle spelling.

Hātan takes accusative thing fæstnesse and accusative name Heofon. Bēo with light is third-singular subjunctive, not the identical imperative spelling; tō tācne is the new bounded dative-function use.
